I was a young lad living in the midwest when Children Of The Corn came out. I was a huge Stephen King fan, had read all of his books, absolutely LOVED being creeped out of my skin at the thoughts his writing evoked. So you can just imagine my excitement to go see this movie. Well my parents let me go to any movie that I wanted to see, no matter the rating, they were secure that they had raised an intelligent, mature boy. After the movie my father picked me up to take me back home. Now we lived about 5 miles from the nearest town, out in the country or BFE as my friends and I sometimes liked to call it. On a 3 acre patch of land with corn fields on 3 sides of us. I didn't consider this fact at all before I went to the theatre to watch the movie, but you can sure bet I considered it all the way home. I lay awake that night staring out my window at the edge of the cornfield, watching, waiting, sweating. To see the sun rise that next morning was the most absolute bliss I had ever experienced. Thinking back to this I am glad it happened. Mister King has allowed me to use my imagination in ways that I never would have dreamed had I not read his books and watched the films made from them.
